principal_papers.title: Effects of strain softening and strength spatial variability on slope failure movement by material point method
principal_papers.verified_location: Section 2(2), Section 3(2); PDF p4 Fig3/Table1 and p5 text/Fig5 visually verified

principal_papers.title: Application of the random material point method to 3D slope failures
principal_papers.geometry: Unnotched 45 deg, 1 m high; 8 m width, 2.5 m crest, 2.5 m beyond toe; grid 0.125 m, 8 points/cell
principal_papers.model: Linear elastic, strain-softening Tresca; implicit DM-G/B-bar
principal_papers.trigger: 99 percent gravity elastic stress initialisation with movement/plasticity prevented; remaining 1 percent released dynamically. Stable cases receive incremented crest foundation weight
principal_papers.boundaries: Base/end fixed, back normal fixed, front free; escaping material points removed
principal_papers.postfailure_evidence: Gravity-only and crest-loaded secondary failures, 15 s endpoint; numerical failed-volume/retrogression comparisons
principal_papers.scope_caveat: Random weak zones/depth trends explicit; no toe excavation/rainfall trigger
principal_papers.implementation_limit: Published 3D realisation costs 12-24 CPU hours; data from authors on request; not a quick deterministic 2D reference
principal_papers.evidence_level: Idealised mechanism investigation; no field validation

additional_verified_scope_boundaries.title: Investigation of retrogressive and progressive slope failure mechanisms using the material point method
additional_verified_scope_boundaries.facts_verified: Publisher indexed introduction/conclusion: short 5 m high slope collapses under self-weight, total-stress cohesion-softening Von Mises, no pore-pressure changes. Long slope uses toe cutting. Field comparison outside paper scope
additional_verified_scope_boundaries.access_limit: Full manuscript unavailable in this pass; do not infer missing geometry/material numbers

additional_verified_scope_boundaries.title: Progressive failure of Aznalcóllar dam using the material point method
additional_verified_scope_boundaries.facts_verified: Construction loading, brittle foundation clay, strain-softening Mohr-Coulomb, coupled flow/deformation. Failure-band geometry matches field observations
additional_verified_scope_boundaries.scope: No toe-excavation trigger described in abstract; not independently confirmed full text. Hydro-mechanical staged-dam case excluded from quick mechanical-only shortlist
additional_verified_scope_boundaries.access_limit: Publisher abstract inspected; geometry/material tables not obtained; no numbers invented
